curriculum.lesson_evidence: Emotive language shapes tone (urgent, hopeful, angry). Ethical persuaders engage feelings without inventing harm or stereotyping groups. Analyse how tone supports or undermines credibility.
curriculum.scope_limit: Proposed Stage 4 NESA English alignment using catalogue outcome codes (EN4-*); content-point mapping and independent NESA verification remain pending.

lesson.child_mission: Emotive language shapes tone (urgent, hopeful, angry). Ethical persuaders engage feelings without inventing harm or stereotyping groups. Analyse how tone supports or undermines credibility.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Revise an overly manipulative line into an engaging but fair emotive line on school waste.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Keeps feeling; removes unfair exaggeration or blame of a group.

CHECK
Assuming any emotion equals bad persuasion. Tone can be fair and felt.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Rewrite a harsh paragraph into two tones (urgent/hopeful) and evaluate credibility of each.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Emotive language shapes tone (urgent, hopeful, angry). Ethical persuaders engage feelings without inventing harm or stereotyping groups. Analyse how tone supports or undermines credibility.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with emotive language, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
'Students are drowning in noise' is emotive metaphor—effective if noise is real; manipulative if exaggerated beyond evidence. Hopeful tone: 'We can build quieter minutes together.'

TRY FIRST

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Keeps feeling; removes unfair exaggeration or blame of a group.
teach_steps.explain:
Emotive language shapes tone (urgent, hopeful, angry). Ethical persuaders engage feelings without inventing harm or stereotyping groups. Analyse how tone supports or undermines credibility.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
